cells.tense: The whole thing is visible from where you stand, and you are putting it into words for someone else.
cells.act: make something skilled and small on the cleared ground
cells.ask: Pick the ground where an old arrangement already came down and build a small piece on it with your own hands — a draft, a list, a first version. Finish it in one sitting, then leave it where whoever it's for can find it.
cells.core: You can stand back from a thing you're inside and see how it all fits together. That's not judgment. It's plain sight of what's true across every layer, and when you explain it, people get through things they were stuck on. It works best when what you understand turns into something you hand over — the picture itself, not just the moment of seeing it. Where it's bending now is at the edges of that. Some of what you've worked out is still unfinished, sitting in your head waiting to be built into something, and a piece of it hasn't been written down yet. So make one part of it real and small. The ground you're building on is already cleared — something false fell there and you know exactly where. No rehearsal. What you hand over, you keep.
cells.sheetLine: You see how it fits, then you say it so it lands.
cells.verb: charting a passage through for others to follow
cells.place: a spot just outside the working, where the whole of it shows at once

cells.tense: You will have worked out the ending of this before anyone has told you the question.
cells.act: engage the hard part on purpose and see what holds
cells.ask: Name the stretch of this that keeps stalling you, and go at it on purpose — one long sitting, no rehearsal. Where it gives, keep it. Where it doesn't, that's your answer about the method, not the aim.
cells.core: Seeing the whole pattern is the gift, and right now it arrives early — you've already worked out how this ends while the others are still asking the first question. You're explaining a crossing before anyone has said they need to make it. The forcing shows most in the quiet hours, when you're still refining something that no longer changes the answer. Here's what that friction is: a test, and a fair one. Put your hands deliberately on the part that keeps stalling and you find out what actually holds — not a verdict on you, information about the shape. Most of a stalled thing is a method that's finished, not a commitment that's failed. Keep the commitment. Drop the method. That's a shorter list than the one you're turning over at night.

cells.tense: The pattern was right there once, and you stopped saying what you saw.
cells.act: act on the private sense of what is right
cells.ask: Something small is yours to do and you've been walking past it. Do it with nobody watching and no explanation afterward — not to anyone, not to yourself. That's the whole instruction.
cells.core: You can still tell how a thing fits together. It's just gone quiet — you see the shape of a situation and you've stopped saying any of it, so the crossing happens without you and you stand back at the rail. What's been missing isn't the sight. It's the plain private sense of what's yours to do about it. That sense doesn't wait on an audience, a plan, or anyone's permission, and it doesn't wait on you being sure first. Choose something unobserved and do it. Not the biggest. The one you've been walking past. Some of what you see is for you before it's for anyone else, and doing it is how the sight gets its footing back.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped saying what you saw and started standing aside.

cells.tense: You are reading the situation accurately and calling none of it your work.
cells.act: choose one connection and flow with it
cells.ask: Go to the person who already knows what you've been working on, and pick the next piece up together instead of alone. The two of you on the same piece, no agenda.
cells.core: You already do this. You see how a thing holds together, explain it, and by the time the person is moving again the guidance has gone anonymous — it belongs to the situation, not to you. Your own account has you as someone who happened to be standing there. The ones who used what you gave them know where it came from; not once have they doubted it. So give the work a second pair of hands. Take what you've been carrying to the one person who already knows its shape, and pick up the next piece together rather than alone. Two readings of the same pattern see more than one, and half of what you've been making sense of was built to be shared before it was finished.

attempts.check: The record does not say the person is a teacher, a guide to anyone specific, or that their knowledge is wanted anywhere — I read 'what you know needs to become what you share' as an existing role, and a reader could rightly say nobody has asked. The ask survives that: finishing the one thing still sitting open is useful whether or not anyone ever receives the explanation, since the seat is about seeing the pattern whole. The sentence serving me more than them is 'you're the one people come to when they can't see the way' — it flatters and it assigns a role the record never gave.
